items.question: How does the role of structural equivalence in the neighborhood-sampling setup of node2vec relate to DeepWalk's advantage when only a small fraction of nodes are labeled for classification?
items.gold_answer: Node2vec's sampling framework explicitly aims to capture structural equivalence by allowing depth-first sampling to reach nodes that can be far apart but play similar structural roles, while DeepWalk shows strong performance when labels are sparse, outperforming baselines even with only 20% labeled nodes and maintaining an advantage at very low training ratios.
items.evidence_quote: Importantly, unlike homophily, structural equivalence does not emphasize connectivity; nodes could be far apart in the network and still have the same structural role.
items.evidence_quote_b: This strong performance when only small fractions of the graph are labeled is a core strength of our approach.

items.question: Compared with BFS and DFS in the neighborhood-sampling method described for node2vec, what kind of graph similarity does DeepWalk's reported performance suggest is especially useful under sparse supervision?
items.gold_answer: BFS is aligned with homophily because it samples immediate neighbors, whereas DFS can capture structural equivalence by moving to farther nodes; DeepWalk's strong results with sparse labels suggest that representations useful for classification can benefit from capturing both local community similarity and structural-role similarity, rather than relying only on immediate-neighbor homophily.
items.evidence_quote: The breadth-first and depth-first sampling represent extreme scenarios in terms of the search space they explore leading to interesting implications on the learned representations.
items.evidence_quote_b: DeepW alkoutperforms all baselines by at least 3% with respect to Micro-F1.

items.question: Under which conditions would the node2vec sampling strategy that explores nodes at increasing distances be more consistent with DeepWalk's gains on Flickr and YouTube: when homophily dominates, or when structural equivalence matters more?
items.gold_answer: The increasing-distance strategy corresponds to DFS, which is more consistent with structural equivalence than homophily; DeepWalk's gains on Flickr and YouTube under very low training ratios indicate that such nonlocal, role-based similarities can be especially helpful when labeled data is scarce.
items.evidence_quote_b: DeepW alksignificantly outperforms the scalable baseline for creating graph representations, EdgeCluster.

items.question: Why is the comparison between BFS and DFS in node2vec relevant when interpreting DeepWalk's results on sparsely labeled graphs such as Flickr and YouTube?
items.gold_answer: Because BFS emphasizes immediate-neighbor homophily while DFS can capture distant nodes with similar structural roles, the comparison helps explain why DeepWalk can remain effective with sparse labels: its learned representations appear robust enough to support classification even when supervision is limited, as shown on Flickr and YouTube.
items.evidence_quote: For example, in Figure 1 for a neighborhood of size k = 3 , BFS samples nodess1,s2,s3.
items.evidence_quote_b: When 1% of the labeled nodes are used for test, the Micro- F1 improves by 14%.
